L-6438 (C-48346, Catrin Lorch): KYC re-run returned VERIFIED. Docs on file (national ID, proof of address, source of funds). PEP: no. Deposit M$6,400 is below the M$10,000 LARGE_CASH threshold, so no report needed. Opened Everyday Current Account A-FB56C7 and posted deposit D-0001 for M$6,400.

L-8674 (C-32803, Javier Mateo Rico Méndez): NOT OPENED. KYC returned INCOMPLETE; missing beneficial_owner_id and beneficial_owner_declaration. Call notes say the account is for and will be funded and operated by Joëlle van Laarhoven, who lives abroad; the applicant would only hold the card. Under §6 the beneficial owner must be identified and verified before opening, and the account cannot be opened in the nominee's name. Also consider whether the deposit source (Joëlle's funds from abroad) needs documenting under §7, and whether the arrangement needs review by Compliance given the nominee-style set-up. Do not open the account until KYC is VERIFIED and BO verification is complete.

- KYC re-run returned VERIFIED. Documents on file cover ID, proof of address and source of funds. She is not a PEP.
- Opened Everyday Current Account **A-FB56C7** and posted the M$6,400 deposit (D-0001).

**L-8674, Javier Mateo Rico Méndez (C-32803): not opened, documents requested.**

That makes him an applicant acting for another person, so under §6 the beneficial owner must be identified and verified before opening. The account also cannot be opened in his name to avoid that.

- I did not open the account and did not book the M$5,100 deposit.
- Once the documents arrive, KYC needs re-running. Because of the nominee-style arrangement, Compliance may also need to review the case. I have not escalated it yet because there is no sanctions or PEP issue, but I can do so if you want.
